about: Controlled vocabulary for the editors' (Polotsky/Böhlig) German statements in the printed Kephalaia edition, and for the transcriber's own commentary. Each German formula is mapped to one id; the id is what the EpiDoc pages carry (@ana="#ed.ID" on gaps, #app.ID on apparatus entries, #tr.ID on commentary paragraphs). The German is kept here as the key to the printed formula; it is never transcribed into the pages. 'reason' is the EpiDoc gap reason the statement implies when it stands outside printed brackets; inside printed brackets the reason is always 'lost'. 'judgement' records how an ambiguous or inconsistent formula was decided, so that every page is encoded alike.

destroyed.judgement: Physical loss of the writing surface. 'vollständig zerstört' (28.24) is the same statement, intensified; one id.

destroyed-almost.judgement: The editors use both wordings (13.14–15 'völlig', 22.4–8 'ganz') for the same statement; one id. Encoded as a loss: the editors give no letters.

destroyed-abraded.judgement: Combination of destruction and abrasion: a loss.

abraded.judgement: Abrasion removes the ink, so the writing is gone rather than merely unreadable: encoded as lost. 'Rest abgerieben' (19.6, 19.13) is the same statement placed after surviving letters; the position in the line carries the 'rest'.

abraded-heavily.judgement: Degree of abrasion; a loss, as 'abgerieben'.

smeared.judgement: Ink is present but blurred: illegible, not lost.

smeared-abraded.judgement: Where abrasion is named the writing counts as lost (rule shared with 'zerstört und abgerieben').

illegible-provisional.judgement: As 'unlesbar'; the editors expected a later reading. Kept apart because it marks passages they meant to revisit.

not-read.judgement: A statement about the editors' work, not about the manuscript: the writing may be legible. Encoded as illegible (nothing given), with the id preserving the difference from 'unlesbar'.

traces.judgement: Ink traces visible but no letters identifiable.

traces-faint.judgement: As 'geringe Spuren', lower degree. Inside printed brackets (21.4) the brackets decide: lost.

uncounted.judgement: The editors print brackets with blank space and no dots: a loss of unknown extent. The width of the blank is typographic and is not converted into a letter count.

open-bracket.en: lost, extent not counted (opening bracket only)
open-bracket.judgement: An opening bracket that is never closed and has nothing restored after it marks a loss of unknown extent: at the line end it runs to the end of the line; at the line start (21.6–11) it marks the lost beginning, and a braced statement beside it describes the rest of the line, which is encoded as a second statement.

open-bracket-query.judgement: Opening bracket followed by a question mark (14.15): a loss to the line end whose existence or extent the editors doubt; encoded with cert=low.

conjecture.en: editors' conjecture (not printed in the text, or an alternative to it)
conjecture.judgement: All forms of proposal are one type; the strength ('man erwartet' vs 'viell.') is kept in the English note. 'Kaum …' (29.13) is a restoration the editors mention and doubt; 'korrigiert; gemeint ist …' (34.8) reports a correction in the manuscript and gives the intended form. Both are proposals not printed in the text: the wording and its strength go in the English note.

correction.judgement: The correction itself is encoded in the text (⟨⟩ supplied-omitted, or the corrected spelling); the apparatus entry records the editors' reading.

confirmation.en: the printed reading is the manuscript's (editors confirm)
confirmation.judgement: Covers the plain 'so' and the softer 'scheint sicher' / 'anscheinend so'; the degree is kept in the note.

uncertain.judgement: Applies to the lemma words; their letters keep whatever sublinear dots the edition prints.

uncertain-strongly.judgement: The three wordings are used interchangeably; one id.

traces-report.en: editors report traces of particular letters
traces-report.judgement: The possible readings derived from the traces are given as readings.

stroke-absent.judgement: The text is encoded without the stroke.

de: Über der Zeile ist etwas nachgetragen
added-above.judgement: Where the editors give the letters, the text carries \x/ (add place=above); 20.25 gives none.

de: von spät. Hd. ü. d. Z.
added-above-later-hand.en: written above the line by a later hand

expunged.en: expunged by the scribe with dots
expunged.judgement: The scribe's own deletion: the edition prints double brackets [[ ]]; encoded ⟦x⟧ (del rend=expunction), not as an editorial surplus. 15.16 adds the cause (dittography from l. 18 by homoioteleuton) in the note. A footnote naming a deletion point ('Tilgungspunkt', 33.12) without printed double brackets is encoded the same way (⟦x⟧). When the editors only think a letter is deleted ('anscheinend getilgt', 33.22) the letter stays in the text as printed and only the apparatus entry records it.

sic.en: kept as transmitted, not understood or a scribal error

running-title.en: the running title differs from the usual one

margin-line.en: one line written in the bottom margin, not given
margin-line.judgement: Printed below the last line in the text block; located at loc='bottom'.

bracket.en: how an unbalanced or cross-line bracket of the edition is encoded

print.en: a printing observation: stroke shape or extent (measured), blur, specks, rules

layout.en: layout: ekthesis, enlarged letters, unmarked blanks, marginal numerals, turnover, chapter opening

reading.en: a letter-identification decision taken on the zoom

source.en: about the source images or the page's context
